# Futu and HKUST Sign Agreement to Advance “AI-Powered Investing” Research


Corporate News


--


Industry-Academia Collaboration to Drive AI Ecosystem Toward “Precision Value Creation”


（Hong Kong, 17 Nov 2026) Futu Holdings Limited ("Futu" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: FUTU), a leading tech-driven digitalized brokerage and wealth management platform, today announced the signing of a collaborative research agreement with the School of Business and Management of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (“HKUST Business School”). The two parties will undertake a one-year in-depth research initiative on “AI-Powered Investing,” examining the impact of AI on users’ information acquisition, trading behaviour, investment decision-making support and platform engagement.


The collaboration marks an important step in Futu’s efforts to advance AI from a tool-driven model toward “precision value creation.” By exploring how AI can more accurately understand the needs of different investor groups, the initiative aims to help users improve information-processing efficiency, strengthen risk awareness and make more informed investment decisions in fast-moving market environments.


Deepening Research to Enable Differentiated Investment Decision-Making Support and Create Greater User Value


The research programme will be conducted in five phases, with the parties planning to jointly publish the findings upon completion. Futu’s AI Growth Center will work with a research team led by Assistant Professor Miaozhe Han of the Department of Information Systems, Business Statistics and Operations Management at the HKUST . The study will conduct quantitative analyses of the practical effectiveness of AI tools across different user segments, subject to stringent requirements for data privacy, data security and compliance requirements.


In today’s fast-changing markets, investors must navigate an ever-growing volume of information, heightened emotional pressures and increasingly complex investment decisions. Futu believes that AI should not merely serve as a broadly accessible tool, but should evolve into an intelligent companion capable of providing differentiated support based on users’ individual characteristics, investment experience and use cases—thereby delivering on the vision of “Smarter Your Money.”


The research team will quantitatively assess the outcomes achieved by different user groups when using AI tools, and evaluate the role of AI across a range of investment scenarios, including information filtering, risk education, research efficiency and decision support. The findings will provide empirical reference for Futu’s future AI technology and business development, supporting the Company’s continued optimisation of product capabilities, resource allocation and ecosystem partnership models. Ultimately, the initiative is expected to enable Futu’s AI services to respond more precisely to the needs of different investors.


This is not the first collaboration between the two teams. In March this year, Futu has collaborated with the HKUST Business School to optimize Futubull AI's feature that intelligently triggers trending questions during market volatility. The project represented an initial exploration of how AI can help users obtain information, formulate questions and better understand market developments at critical market moments.


The initial results validated the feasibility of integrating academic insights into real-world user scenarios, laying the groundwork for this more systematic “AI-Powered Investing” research initiative. The collaboration is now evolving from the optimisation of a single feature to a comprehensive research framework encompassing information acquisition, trading behaviour, investment decision-making support and platform engagement, marking a further deepening of industry-academia-research collaboration.


From left: Vincent Yao, Head of AI Application R&D Centerof Futu; Daniel Tse, Managing Director of Futu Securities; Professor Kai‐Lung Hui, Elman Family Professor of Business at HKUST; and Miaozhe Han, Assistant Professor at HKUST Business School


Professor Kai‐Lung Hui, Elman Family Professor of Business at HKUST,


said: “AI is driving lots of changes in our society, but how it affects people's investment attitude and strategy is a nascent research area that calls for quality field data and experience. It is our distinct pleasure to collaborate with Futu, one of the most forward looking digital platforms that has transformed the personal investment regime. Through this collaboration, we will explore how people manage their wealth under the influence of AI and ways to enhance the welfare of investors, firms, and the market.”


Vincent Yao, Head of Futu’s AI Application R&D Center


, said: “We are delighted to collaborate with the HKUST Business School once again. Building on the encouraging results of our earlier optimisation project, we are joining forces to advance this research and more clearly identify the priorities for differentiated AI enablement across various user groups. These include helping investors filter out irrelevant information, strengthening risk education, improving research efficiency and providing decision support. We look forward to seeing this research advance Futu’s AI ecosystem from broad-based application toward ‘precision value creation,’ as we continue to enhance the investment experience through technology and create sustainable, long-term value for investors.”


Building on HK$30 Million Donation Partnership to Support Hong Kong’s Innovation and Talent Development


Earlier this year, Futu donated HK$30 million to HKUST to support the University’s efforts in advancing innovative research, facilitating the translation of research outcomes and establishing scholarships to recognise outstanding HKUST students. This research initiative not only further extends the existing partnership between Futu and HKUST, but also marks a new phase in their joint efforts to promote the integration of industry, academia and research.


The donation and scholarship programme represent neither a one-off contribution nor the conclusion of the partnership. Rather, it marks the beginning of Futu’s ongoing commitment to higher education, research innovation and talent development.


Through this collaboration, Futu will combine HKUST’s academic research strengths with its own industry experience to explore the application potential of frontier technologies in financial services. The Company will also seek to engage leading AI and data talent, building long-term capabilities to support future technological advancement.


As a Hong Kong-based, globally oriented fintech company, Futu will continue to leverage its strengths in financial technology, AI, data applications and industry practice. Through deeper collaboration with more local universities and research teams, Futu aims to promote the deeper integration of AI and financial services, while contributing sustained momentum to Hong Kong’s innovation and technology ecosystem and the development of professional talent.
